selector.champion: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
selector.rationale: Patient has a history of NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (<25%) and presented with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, which is consistent with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome is also a strong candidate due to the presence of delta waves and alternating QRS complex morphologies, but the patient's history and presentation are more consistent with heart failure.

rejected.why: No evidence of acute cardiopulmonary processes on chest radiograph and no paradoxical pulse or blood pressure
